description.summary: Hybrid Retrieval combines lexical and vector retrieval so a RAG system can use exact term matching and semantic similarity together.
description.description: Hybrid Retrieval is a RAG technique that queries more than one retrieval signal, commonly a keyword retriever and a dense vector retriever, then combines the candidate results before generation.
description.problemStatement: A single retrieval method can miss relevant context when the query depends on exact terminology, semantic paraphrase, or both.
description.coreIdea: Run complementary retrievers and merge their ranked candidates so downstream context assembly can choose from a broader evidence pool.

inputRequirements.name: Queryable corpus index
inputRequirements.description: At least two retrieval indexes or retriever configurations are needed to combine retrieval signals.

outputArtifacts.name: Merged ranked candidates
outputArtifacts.description: A candidate set produced by combining results from lexical and semantic retrieval.

implementationConsiderations: Use a deterministic merge strategy so evaluation can compare retrieval configurations.
evaluationGuidance: Compare recall-oriented retrieval metrics before and after combining lexical and semantic results.
